what: H9-P1 pre-seal edge RE-CERT at flight epoch. Freeze condition (whisper c5003): edges PINNED n4/n6/n8, 'fly-those-or-re-cert-$0-at-flight-epoch'. Pinned 2026-07-24; re-certed 2026-08-07 (14 days).
method: READ-ONLY backend.target calibration on ibm_marrakesh; re-ran pick_layouts (the SAME selector that set the pins) and priced pinned vs today under pick_layouts' own metric (2q error + both readout errors). No circuits submitted.
result: RE-CERT FIRES. Zero overlap at every rung; pinned edges are 3.8-7.3x worse than today's best.

selftest_at_frozen_sizing.note: Q two-copy rate 0.9517 (n4) / 0.9507 (n6) vs target (1+a^2)/2=0.9512; delivery-integrity shots1+fresh_per_row+manifest_P_indep all True

reading: Turnover alone would only say the pins are no longer OPTIMAL. The COST RATIO is what makes it decision-relevant: flying the frozen pins today would fly the two-copy Bell arm on edges ~4-7x worse than available, and the whole claim rests on the MEASURED two-copy rate. NOT claimed here: a precise predicted rate degradation - that needs the full circuit+noise model, and I am not going to manufacture a number for it.
recommendation: Re-cert to today's edges before seal, which the freeze's own condition explicitly permits. Re-run this at the actual submit epoch - 14 days of drift produced total turnover, so hours matter less than days but the check is $0 and should gate the seal every time.
does_not_touch: alpha=0.95, all-Paulis draw, shots=1 fresh-per-row, C1 covering decoder, determinism red-team, C1 freeze 408/4482/55589, grader. Apparatus only.

addendum_whisper_6169_conventional_arm.ask: Whisper #6169: my re-cert priced the QUANTUM edges only; price the conventional arm too and confirm the flight takes both pick_layouts returns at the same epoch.
addendum_whisper_6169_conventional_arm.finding_1_same_epoch: CONFIRMED. exp142_flight_kit.py:349 does `q_layout, conv_layout, bell_pairs = pick_layouts(backend, n)` — ONE call, one calibration read, both arms. conv_layout is recorded into the manifest (line 352). addendum_whisper_6169_conventional_arm.finding_2_no_conv_pin_exists: The requested pinned-vs-today comparison is UNAVAILABLE: results/p1_kit_confirm.json records ONLY pinned_edges. No conventional pin was ever taken. The Jul-24 pin was ASYMMETRIC from the start — quantum edges pinned, conventional qubits not.

finding_3_asymmetry_runs_AGAINST_the_qua.reading: The CONVENTIONAL arm sits on ~2.3-2.8x BETTER readout than the quantum arm's qubits. Structural, not chosen: conv_layout takes the n global min-readout qubits, while the quantum arm must take DISJOINT COUPLED PAIRS and therefore cannot cherry-pick readout. The apparatus advantages the COMPETITOR.

addendum_whisper_6169_conventional_arm.consequence_for_whispers_worry: Whisper's concern was that re-certing only the quantum arm would rebuild F119's quantum-honest-vs-classical-naive asymmetry in the apparatus. The concern is correct in form but the sign is inverted here: the standing asymmetry FAVORS the classical arm, and flying the Jul-24 pins literally would have flown STALE quantum edges against FRESH conventional qubits — self-harm, not gate-shopping. Re-certing both at one epoch REDUCES the asymmetry rather than creating one.
addendum_whisper_6169_conventional_arm.not_claimed: That this fully neutralizes the arms. Readout is one axis; the quantum arm additionally carries 2q gate error the conventional arm does not, which is priced in the main re-cert and is why the quantum arm needs good EDGES not just good readout.
